title: CompTIA Linux+ (XK0-005)
summary: CompTIA Linux+, exam code XK0-005, is a vendor neutral certification for administrators who already support Linux servers and want to prove it formally. It sits at a professional level, above the entry level IT certifications and alongside the server and network administrator exams, and it assumes hands on time at a command line. Passing it tells an employer that you can manage users, storage, services and permissions, harden a host, automate routine work with scripts, and diagnose faults without a graphical interface. The exam is proctored and mixes multiple choice and multiple response questions with performance based items that ask you to complete a task in a simulated environment. It leads to roles such as Linux administrator, systems administrator, cloud support engineer and site reliability technician. The domain list below follows the published objectives, so check the current version with CompTIA before booking. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CompTIA.

beginner.definition: This is a professional certificate from CompTIA about Linux. Linux is the family of open source operating systems used on most servers. It is an intermediate exam, which means it expects real practice at a text command line. The exam code is XK0-005, and some questions ask you to complete a task.
beginner.whyItMatters: Web servers, cloud platforms and network appliances mostly run Linux. Companies need people who can keep those machines secure and working. This certificate shows you can do that work by hand, without a mouse or a control panel. It fits help desk staff who want to move up, and it supports later cloud and security certifications. Employers often treat it as proof of practical skill rather than theory.
howItWorks: Install Linux on a spare computer or a virtual machine, because you learn more when you can break it.
Practise the everyday tasks, such as creating users, setting permissions, mounting storage and managing services.
Learn a scripting language, because automation is a large part of the job and of the exam.
Study security topics such as file permissions, firewalls and mandatory access control, and apply them on your own host.
Practise troubleshooting by breaking something on purpose and reading the log files to find the cause.
Take practice tests, then sit the proctored exam, which includes task based items in a simulated system.
beginner.example: Picture a shared office kitchen with a locked cupboard. Every colleague needs a key for the cupboard. Only the manager should change who holds one. If the keys are copied carelessly, anyone can take the expensive coffee machine. On a Linux server the same idea appears as file permissions and user groups. Each file states who may read, write or run it. A Linux administrator decides who gets which key.
takeaways: You cannot pass this exam by reading alone, because several questions require practical actions.
Learn the command line slowly and correctly, because small typing errors cause real outages.
Confirm the current exam version and objectives on the CompTIA website before you book a date.

objectives: Administer users, groups, permissions and services on a Linux host
Configure storage, file systems and network settings from the command line
Harden a Linux system by applying access control, firewall and patching practices
Write shell scripts that automate repetitive administration tasks
Use containers and configuration management tools to deploy and manage workloads
Diagnose and resolve faults in storage, networking, services and application behaviour

chapters.title: System management
objectives: Install and configure a Linux distribution and explain the boot process that starts it
Create, modify and remove user accounts and groups, and manage password and login policy
Set file ownership, permissions and special permission bits so that access matches policy
Partition and format storage, mount file systems and manage logical volumes
Manage disk space, quotas and swap, and explain the difference between each one
Start, stop and inspect system services and scheduled jobs, and read their logs
Configure hostname, time, locale and network interface settings on a running system

chapters.title: Security
objectives: Apply the principle of least privilege when creating accounts, groups and service users
Configure a host firewall and explain which traffic the rules allow or deny
Use mandatory access control frameworks to confine a process even if it is compromised
Identify common authentication methods, including key based login and central directory services
Detect and respond to suspicious local activity by reading authentication and system logs
Apply hardening steps such as removing unused packages and restricting remote access

chapters.title: Scripting, containers and automation
objectives: Write a shell script with variables, conditionals, loops and clear error handling
Process text files with standard tools to extract, compare and summarise data
Schedule scripts and other tasks so that routine work happens without a person
Use version control to track configuration and script changes and to review them
Install, run and inspect a container image and explain how it differs from a virtual machine
Apply configuration management so that many hosts keep the same declared settings

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
objectives: Apply a structured troubleshooting method that starts from the symptom a user reports
Diagnose storage faults such as a full file system, a failing disk or a broken mount
Diagnose network faults such as a wrong route, a name resolution failure or a blocked port
Diagnose service and resource problems, including high processor, memory or input output load
Interpret system and application log entries to locate the origin of an error
Restore a degraded or unbootable system and document what caused the failure
Escalate a fault with the evidence that the next team needs to continue the work
